review: See docs/handoff/security-2026-09/client-lifetime.html for input/result categories, uncached operations and local state ownership. Every changed mutation-capable module requires renewed sensitivity review. Self-configuration preparation and rollout review retain only revision, generation, request ID and plan digest metadata; factor codes remain in sensitive local state and factor responses bypass mutation caches. Hashes were re-pinned after merging origin/main: the design-system migration (routes moved onto the shared ui primitives Dialog/Menu/Alert/Button/Select and helpers) and the react/set-state-in-effect refactor (resets moved from effects to useResetOnChange, seeded useState, or key-based remounts) both changed module bytes without adding a mutation surface, cache boundary, or plaintext ownership. Literal NUL bytes accidentally written into signature template literals were replaced with the \u0000 escape (no runtime change). The sensitivity posture is unchanged. The login challenge passkey leg (api/stepup useLoginChallengePasskey) mirrors usePasskeyLogin: no cache, no retained result. The sign-in enrolment gate (#785, routes/EnrolmentGate + ui/auth/SecondFactorSetup) holds the re-proved password in component sensitive state until it is handed to the recovery-code mutation, whose guarded account-session transfer carries it with the codes across that one remint (retirement would otherwise wipe it) so the factor enrolment that follows can present it; the gate releases the password once an authenticator enrolment starts, and both die with the gate. useRegenerateRecoveryCodes and the gate share one handoff (useRecoveryCodeHandoff). Storybook coverage pass (feat/storybook-coverage): routes/MachineAccess and routes/ScimProvisioning changed by `export` keywords only (page, dialog and card components) so stories can mount them; no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Federated sign-up (#607): api/session useOIDCLogin carries the login intent and the addressed org into the OIDC start body (no credential material, no cache); api/account adds the `?org=` door read; api/settings and routes/InstanceAdmin add the org origin filter to a read; routes/Login feeds the staged card (ui/auth/LoginForm, #800) the open door and the intent, and the card keeps the password in the same component sensitive state behind its password step; api/values names the remedy when a reauth start is refused for a provider without an assurance policy. No new retained state, cache boundary or plaintext ownership. Docstring pass (#607, CodeRabbit-generated, reviewed): api/account, api/session, api/settings, api/values and routes/Login changed in doc comments only; no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Provider identity (#804, CodeRabbit): routes/Login and ui/auth/LoginForm key the sign-in card's provider by kind and slug, in the row started, its busy state and the last-used badge, so a SAML and an OIDC provider sharing a slug stay distinct; the same two mutations start with the same arguments, and no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. LoginForm: the shown step is derived by shownStage; a confirmation whose provider the refreshed sign-up door no longer admits falls back to the door instead of a blank card. No mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Delivery-target reporting (#790): routes/MachineAccess reads the per-environment delivery-target listings (api/deliveryTargets, query only, no values) and the grant dialog adds `report-delivery-status` beside `read` through the existing grant mutation via createGrantsSequentially; the grant warning's key list takes tabIndex so its scroll region is keyboard-reachable; api/identities scopeOf tracks `report-delivery-status` per environment and grantableFor offers it wherever it is not held, so the grant dialog can add it on its own to an account that already reads (it makes no key reachable and needs no catalogue read or disclosure ceremony); the Kubernetes tab reads `/meta` protocol_capabilities and issues no list call on a server that does not advertise delivery-target-report; the grant dialog reads the same cached `/meta` query (api/deliveryTargets useReportingSupport) and does not offer `report-delivery-status` on such a server; the dialog gates the atom on whoami's server-computed `delivery_report_grant` hint (passed down from the page's useAuth) and on `/meta`, and reads no org membership listing, so opening it records no membership read or denial; while a grant is in flight the dialog keeps GrantBody (and its navigation guard) mounted even if the refreshed scope leaves nothing to widen, and a failed grant keeps it mounted so the uncertain result stays on screen, and its formula names org- or instance-scope manage-members for the report atom; scopeOf carries report-delivery-status origins; no new mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership. SSH certificates (#155): api/ssh adds CA, profile and certificate hooks; the three calls that carry key material are plain async functions, never cached mutations: createSSHCA and rotateSSHCA send an optional pasted CA private key (write-only, dropped from dialog state whatever the outcome, never retried), and issueSSHCertificate returns a generated user private key through parsedPick into the shared display-once mint lifecycle (routes/SSHCertificates, masked at the same session and route boundaries as a lease password, with the stored-confirmation gate). Profile, retire, delete and revoke hooks are useMutation over public metadata only. routes/MachineAccess mounts the SSHCertificatesPanel as a new tab and passes the session, environments and requester candidates; no other mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. SSH transport (#155, CodeRabbit): api/ssh spreads the workspace transport into every SDK call; the three key-material functions (createSSHCA, rotateSSHCA, issueSSHCertificate) and sshTrustedKeys take it as a required argument, which routes/SSHCertificates supplies from useTransport(), and the same-origin KRL link is not offered inside a workspace. The same calls carry the same values; no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Private PKI (#154): api/pki.ts adds the issuer, profile and certificate hooks. Issuer and profile mutations carry only public material (names, policies, PEM certificates and chains); a CA private key is never entered in the SPA (import is CLI-only). A CSR issuance is an ordinary mutation (a CSR and a certificate are public). A generated-key issuance is the plain async issueGeneratedCertificate (parsedPick of certificate and private_key_pem), never a mutation, and routes/CertificatesTab holds the display-once key in useSensitiveState behind the mint passkey ceremony, with a navigation guard until the operator confirms it is stored. routes/MachineAccess gained the Certificates tab and routes/InstanceAdmin the two PKI panels; neither adds a cache boundary or plaintext ownership. api/access.ts only lists the issue-certificate atom in the capability registry; no mutation surface changed. PR #822 main integration reviewed: Cloudflare provider and destination metadata use existing adapter forms; bearer credentials remain in useSensitiveState and uncached useSensitiveMutation. Sealed-webhook response identity remains supported. PR #825 integration review: MachineAccess mounts both existing SSHCertificatesPanel and CertificatesTab, passing the same session, environment and principal context; generated PKI keys remain owned by CertificatesTab sensitive state, with no new parent cache or secret lifetime. Transit integration: api/access adds crypto-use and crypto-manage beside issue-certificate in the capability metadata registry; no secret state, mutation transport or cache ownership changes. Temporary access (#152): api/temporaryAccess adds uncached mutations for access policies and requests whose bodies carry capability names, durations, principal ids and a free-text reason (no credential or value material, no retained result beyond the query invalidation); routes/TemporaryAccess holds only those fields in ordinary component state; routes/Ceremony and api/values add the closed `access` purpose to the existing passkey ceremony, with the TOTP code still in sensitive state and no new cache boundary. Review round (#152): api/temporaryAccess splits the ordinary request body (duration required) from the emergency body (duration optional); same fields, no new cache boundary or plaintext ownership. Reviewed CodeRabbit documentation-only updates to temporaryAccess, Ceremony and TemporaryAccess: no runtime, mutation transport, cache or sensitive-state ownership changes. Combined AWS provider UI review: AWS descriptor and credentials remain in sensitive state and uncached mutations. Provider switching clears both. Vault and Cloudflare routing and provider-aware labels are retained; other reviews are inherited from the integrated stack. GitLab integration retains explicit tri-state protection flags, weakening ceremonies and sensitive credential state alongside AWS and other providers. Combined adapter form reviewed; credentials remain uncached and provider switches clear sensitive access state. Imported final PKI docstring sensitivity review: comment-only edits preserve credential state and mutation boundaries. AWS move resume review: MoveDetail passes the existing adapter provider to OriginMoveForm so resumed AWS credentials use the same local sensitive access state and uncached descriptor mutation as initial origin moves; no new secret lifetime or cache boundary. Final lower-stack review: PKI renewal invalidates certificate listings after success or failure without retaining private material; temporary-access approval eligibility remains server-calculated metadata, with no new credential cache or sensitive-state lifetime. Integration review: retained GitLab forms and capabilities alongside PKI loading guards and AWS move-provider availability. Generated keys remain in existing sensitive component state; credentials use existing uncached mutation boundaries. Member access rules stage C: api/rules.ts adds useQuery listings (rules, key catalogues via listKeys, never values) and two useMutation hooks whose bodies carry a principal id, a capability name and a Where of project, environment and key ids and folder paths; results are rule metadata, nothing retained beyond query invalidation and a session refresh. routes/Members.tsx mounts the rule editor, Who can reach one key? and the glossary over that metadata in ordinary component state. The key folder move paths (api/matrix useUpdateKeyMetadata, api/catalogue useMoveKeysToFolders, definitions apply) add `confirm_widening`, a list of principal ids echoed from the server's 409 `widening`; no credential or value material, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed. Key-declaration permission gate (can_declare_keys): routes/ImportWizard takes a canDeclareKeys prop and skips new-key declaration when it is false, the same branch Git mode already took; no mutation surface, cache boundary or plaintext ownership changed.
